behavioral_effects: First live Stop-hook firing found the defect; committed work no longer re-blocks turn-end
gitutil gains toplevel() so porcelain answers are only trusted for the root they describe
compatibility_impact: Stop-check blocks strictly less often: only touched paths still dirty in the working tree count, and change records anywhere in the dirty tree satisfy the record rule; the conservative all-touches-dirty behavior is retained when git is unavailable or answers for an enclosing repository
limitations: The live-firing also revealed hooks activate immediately in this environment rather than at next session start - the Phase 3 checklist can run sooner than planned
reason: First live firing of the Stop hook produced a false positive: it blocked on files already committed in governed commits with change records, because the touched log is session-scoped memory that outlives commits and never sees records written by the governance CLI subprocess rather than the agent's Edit tool. The touched log is evidence of what a session did, not of what remains unaccounted for - only still-dirty paths may block
rollback: git revert restores the previous session-memory-only behavior and its false positive
security_impact: None - read-only git queries; one new rev-parse --show-toplevel call
summary: stop-check: reconcile the touched log against git state before blocking

validators_run.evidence_ref: 109 tests green - 2 new tests pin committed-touch reconciliation and CLI-written record counting; the minimal-repo conservative path re-pinned under the toplevel guard
